spec: Write iniconf.py with `load(text: str) -> dict` that turns INI text into a nested dict {section: {key: value}}. Rules: `[name]` starts a section (name stripped); keys before any section go in "DEFAULT"; lines whose first non-space char is ; or # are comments; `key = value` or `key: value` splits on the first = or :, key is lower-cased and stripped, value stripped; an indented non-empty line continues the previous value (joined with \n); a repeated section merges, a repeated key overwrites. After parsing, each non-DEFAULT section inherits DEFAULT keys it does not define. Then values are expanded: `${key}` refers to the same section (falling back to DEFAULT), `${section:key}` to another section, `$$` is a literal $; expansion is recursive, and a missing reference or a cycle raises ValueError. Finally coerce: yes/no/true/false/on/off (any case) -> bool, plain integers -> int, other text stays str. Raise ValueError for a line that is neither a section, comment, blank, continuation nor key/value. The result includes the DEFAULT section only if it has keys. Standard library only (do not use configparser).
